x: Article 40, a Directive Principle, tells the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government. Articles 243A, 243B and 243G came much later with the 73rd Amendment.
t: Discriminate Article 40 (directive) from Part IX (the 73rd Amendment).

x: Option B is incorrect: the 1919 Act made local self-government a transferred subject under dyarchy, run by elected Ministers, not a reserved one. The other statements are correct.
t: Discriminate reserved from transferred subjects.

x: Both are true: local self-government is democratic decentralisation precisely because it brings people's participation and accountability to the local level. R explains A.
t: Ask whether participation and accountability explain decentralisation.

x: Balwant Rai Mehta proposed three tiers, Ashok Mehta two tiers and Nyaya Panchayats, Hanumantha Rao district planning, and L.M. Singhvi constitutional status. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each committee to its key recommendation.

x: The Madras Corporation came first (1688), then Ripon's Resolution (1882), the 1919 Act and Rajasthan's Panchayati Raj (1959). The order is A, B, C, D.
t: Recall the years 1688, 1882, 1919 and 1959.

x: The 73rd Amendment covers rural bodies and came into force on 24 April 1993. The 74th covers urban bodies and came into force on 1 June 1993. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Pair the 73rd with Panchayats (24 April) and the 74th with towns (1 June).

x: All four are correct: the 73rd Amendment added Part IX (Articles 243–243-O) and the 74th added Part IX-A (Articles 243P–243ZG).
t: Recall the Article ranges of Parts IX and IX-A.

x: The Gram Panchayat works at village level, the Panchayat Samiti at block level, and the Zila Parishad at district level. A Nagar Panchayat governs an area changing from rural to urban. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each level to its body.

x: A is true: under Article 243A, the Gram Sabha is all the voters on the village roll. R is false because the elected executive is the Gram Panchayat, not the Gram Sabha.
t: Discriminate the Gram Sabha (all voters) from the Gram Panchayat (elected body).

x: Three are local functions: public health, sanitation and water supply. Judicial review belongs to the higher courts.
t: Find the function that belongs to the courts.

x: Under Article 243B, States with a population of 20 lakh or less need not have the intermediate tier.
t: Recall the 20-lakh exemption.

x: Option C is incorrect: under Article 243J, the State Legislature, not Parliament, provides for keeping and auditing Panchayat accounts.
t: Recall who makes the laws on Panchayat audit.

x: Rajasthan was first, starting Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959. Andhra Pradesh was second.
t: Recall Nagaur, 2 October 1959.

x: I, II and III are correct: the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957), the 'architect of Panchayati Raj', and the G.V.K. Rao Committee (1985) on revival. IV is false because L.M. Singhvi was 1986; 1977–78 was Ashok Mehta.
t: Recall the years of the Panchayati Raj committees.

x: Both are true: the State Election Commission conducts local elections, and the Governor sets up a State Finance Commission every five years. They are separate bodies, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether one body's role explains another's.

x: Article 243A covers the Gram Sabha, 243-I the State Finance Commission, 243J audit, and 243ZD the District Planning Committee. The answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.
t: Recall the Articles of Part IX and IX-A.

x: Lord Ripon is called the father of local self-government in India because of his Resolution of 1882. Metcalfe called villages 'little republics'.
t: Recall Ripon's 1882 Resolution.

x: The 11th Schedule lists 29 subjects for Panchayats and the 12th lists 18 for municipalities. Part IX is rural and Part IX-A urban. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Pair the 11th Schedule (29, rural) with the 12th (18, urban).

x: Both are true: the District Planning Committee comes under Article 243ZD and the Metropolitan Planning Committee under Article 243ZE.
t: Recall Articles 243ZD and 243ZE.

x: Under Article 243C, the State Legislature decides the composition of Panchayats, and Article 243R does so for municipalities.
t: Remember that local bodies are a State subject.

x: Both are true: the minimum age to contest Panchayat and municipal elections is 21, and Articles 243C and 243R deal with their composition. The key treats those Articles as the source of the age rule, so R explains A.
t: Recall the minimum age of 21.

x: Option A is incorrect: at least one-third of seats and chairpersons' posts must be reserved for women, under Articles 243D (Panchayats) and 243T (municipalities).
t: Recall the one-third minimum for women.

x: I and II are correct: after early dissolution, elections must be held within six months, unless less than six months of the term remain. III is false because the term is five years.
t: Recall the five-year term and the six-month rule.

x: Three are correct: Panchayats and municipalities have five-year terms, under Articles 243E and 243U. Statement 3 is false because no election is needed if less than six months remain.
t: Recall the six-month exception.

x: Article 243D covers reservations, 243E tenure, 243G powers, and 243-I the State Finance Commission. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall Articles 243D, 243E, 243G and 243-I.

x: Option D is incorrect: judicial review is not a local function. Local bodies handle subjects like economic development, social justice, sanitation, health, and roads and bridges.
t: Find the function that belongs to the courts.

x: All three are correct: Article 243G covers Panchayats' powers and 243W municipalities', and water supply and local utilities are among their functions.
t: Pair Article 243G (Panchayats) with 243W (municipalities).

x: Both are true: the State Finance Commission is under Article 243-I for Panchayats and Article 243-Y for municipalities.
t: Pair Article 243-I (Panchayats) with 243-Y (municipalities).

x: Article 243W covers municipalities' powers, 243Y the Finance Commission, 243Z audit, and 243ZE the Metropolitan Planning Committee. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the Articles of Part IX-A.

x: Both are true: local self-government is democratic decentralisation through elected bodies, so it is neither central control nor mere administration.
t: Recall what local self-government means.

x: The Hanumantha Rao Committee on district planning was set up in 1983. G.V.K. Rao was 1985 and L.M. Singhvi 1986.
t: Recall the years of the Panchayati Raj committees.

x: Both are true: the 73rd and 74th Amendments were passed in 1992, and 24 April, the day the 73rd took effect in 1993, is National Panchayati Raj Day.
t: Recall National Panchayati Raj Day.

x: All three are correct: under the 74th Amendment, a smaller urban area has a Municipal Council and a larger one a Municipal Corporation, and both systems connect to district planning.
t: Recall the three kinds of urban body.

x: The three-tier structure is compulsory under Article 243B, though States under 20 lakh may skip the middle tier. It is a constitutional requirement, not just an administrative choice.
t: Recall that three tiers are compulsory, with one exemption.

x: Only one is correct: local bodies handle rural development. Public order is a State function, and Panchayat audit laws are made by the State Legislature, not the CAG or the Collector.
t: Check each statement for the right authority.
